title: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation · Paper 1 (SL) — original full-format practice
subject: mathematics-applications-interpretation
instructions: An approved graphing calculator is required. Answer every question in its digital working area, preserving intermediate steps, units and graphs. No separate answer sheet is used.

resources.label: Original data set — commute and study time
resources.text:
Six students recorded daily commute time x (minutes) and evening study time y (minutes):
A: 12, 94
B: 18, 86
C: 25, 82
D: 33, 69
E: 41, 63
F: 55, 48

questions.label: Question 1 — finance
questions.prompt: A student deposits 6000 yuan in an account paying 3.2% annual interest compounded monthly. Find the balance after 4 years and the first month in which the balance exceeds 7000 yuan.

questions.label: Question 2 — statistics
questions.prompt: Use the commute data to find Pearson’s correlation coefficient and the least-squares regression line of y on x. Interpret the slope in context.

questions.label: Question 3 — modelling
questions.prompt: A water tank initially contains 1200 L and drains at a rate modelled by V(t) = 1200(0.93)^t, where t is measured in minutes. Find the volume after 15 minutes and the time at which 75% of the original water has drained.

questions.label: Question 4 — geometry
questions.prompt: A wheelchair ramp rises 0.84 m over a horizontal distance of 10.5 m. Calculate its angle of elevation and its length. A guideline limits the angle to 5°. Decide whether the ramp satisfies the guideline.

questions.label: Question 5 — networks
questions.prompt: A delivery network has vertices A, B, C, D and E with edge weights AB 7, AC 4, BC 3, BD 6, CD 5, CE 8 and DE 2. Use Kruskal's algorithm to find a minimum spanning tree and its total weight.

questions.label: Question 6 — probability distributions
questions.prompt: The number of customers arriving in ten minutes follows a Poisson distribution with mean 3.4. Find the probability of at least five arrivals and the smallest number n such that P(X ≤ n) > 0.95.

questions.label: Question 7 — sinusoidal modelling
questions.prompt: A daylight model is D(t) = a sin(b(t − c)) + d hours. Given a maximum of 15.2 hours at day 172 and a minimum of 8.8 hours at day 355, determine a, b, c and d and estimate D(80).

questions.label: Question 8 — Voronoi diagram
questions.prompt: Three emergency stations are at A(1,2), B(9,2) and C(5,8). Find equations of the perpendicular bisectors and determine the region closest to C. Decide which station serves P(4,4).

questions.label: Question 9 — numerical methods
questions.prompt: Use technology to solve 2e^(−0.3x) = 0.2x + 0.5. Explain the meaning of each intersection if the two sides model supply and demand in hundreds of units.

questions.label: Question 10 — bivariate statistics
questions.prompt: A regression model y = 1.72x + 14.6 has r = 0.81 for x between 10 and 40. Estimate y at x = 32, explain the meaning of r², and evaluate using the model at x = 75.

questions.label: Question 11 — calculus with technology
questions.prompt: The profit from selling x hundred tickets is P(x) = −2.4x³ + 18x² + 12x − 40. Find all stationary points in 0 ≤ x ≤ 8 and determine the ticket quantity giving maximum profit.
